notes.text: It is considered impolite to ask someone else if the "want" to do something.  Instead, use the negative form of the verb in a question.
notes.html: It is considered impolite to ask someone else if the "want" to do something.  Instead, use the negative form of the verb in a question.

notes.text:
Very important: "tai" can only be used for the I person, like "i want". 

If you want to say that someone else wants, you use "tagaru". 

Ex:かれは牛乳を飲みたがっています。

This is because Japanese never imply they know what someone else wishes, and "garu" means: "i think that", "i heard that", etc.
notes.html:
Very important: "tai" can only be used for the I person, like "i want".
If you want to say that someone else wants, you use "tagaru".
Ex:かれは牛乳を飲みたがっています。
This is because Japanese never imply they know what someone else wishes, and "garu" means: "i think that", "i heard that", etc.

examples.body_text:
日本に行きたいです。 

		(I) want to go to Japan.
examples.body_html:
日本に行きたいです。 
(I) want to go to Japan.

examples.japanese: 君のところへ行きたいよ。
examples.body_text:
君のところへ行きたいよ。 

		(I) 
		want to go 
		to where you are.
examples.body_html:
君のところへ行きたいよ。 
(I) want to go to where you are.

examples.japanese: 日本で英語をおしえたいです。
examples.body_text:
日本で英語をおしえたいです。 

		I want to teach English in Japan.
examples.body_html:
日本で英語をおしえたいです。 
I want to teach English in Japan.
